═══ SESSION: 5e75 CLOSED, 77ed/7a79 ATTESTED FROM ONE RUN, 48b3 UNBLOCKED — and the store lock is
now a real contention hazard from CONCURRENT sessions ═══
Worktrees: rebar-wt-provider-seam (store ops), rebar-wt-48b3impl (the 48b3+77ed stack).

## STATE: 25 closed / 3 in_progress / 7 open  (was 23 / 5 / 7)
CLOSED THIS SESSION: 5e75, 7a79.
in_progress: 48b3 + 77ed (both code-ready and green, NOT yet pushed to Gerrit), d5c7 (decision pending).

## THE HIGH-LEVERAGE MOVE: ONE review-plan RUN SETTLED THREE TICKETS
5e75's close gate demanded a fresh review (stale-material after the AC3 edit). 77ed and 7a79 each
needed a live-run attestation. Those are the SAME artifact, so one run served all three:
  rebar review-plan 5e75-522e-70d1-4363   with REBAR_USAGE_LOG exported
  tree origin/main @ 144bb02251, verdict PASS, blocking 0, signed; signed_at 1785701669109051000
  logs: $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/{review_run2.log, usage_run2.jsonl}
Do this deliberately next time — an attestation run and a gate-refresh run are interchangeable.

FIRST ATTEMPT WAS KILLED at a 10-minute foreground timeout, but its usage log had ALREADY captured 8
finder rows — the attestation survived the kill. Run these in the BACKGROUND; review-plan takes
~5.5 min of LLM time and a close takes longer.

## 77ed — SATISFIED. The Pass-1 finder demonstrably runs on OPUS again.
Usage log by (step, model_class, model):
  5 x (finders, frontier, anthropic:claude-opus-4-8)      <- Pass-1
  1 x (verify, -, sonnet)  1 x (coach_notes, -, sonnet)   <- Pass-2 / Pass-4
The run cfg IS sonnet (verdict envelope says so), which is what makes this discriminating: pre-b690
the finder would have inherited sonnet. Prereq-window test also landed and was RE-mutation-checked
ON THIS TREE (model=None at prerequisites.py:187 -> RED, restore -> GREEN) rather than trusting the
pre-merge proof.

## 7a79 — ATTESTED, with the literal-vs-intent gap RECORDED not papered over
Classifying all 37 usage rows against the 4096 floor:
  28 rows BELOW floor, zero/zero -> pre-fix these each warned (~20/run per the docstring). NOW ZERO.
   7 rows caching WORKED -> zero warnings.
   2 rows ABOVE floor, genuinely zero/zero -> 2 warnings, and grep confirms EXACTLY 2 in the run.
So FALSE POSITIVES WENT 28 -> 0. Aggregate cache_write_tokens 32509, cache_read 292816.
The AC says "zero cache warnings WHEN CACHING IS WORKING" — met on its own precondition; not met on a
bare-literal reading, because two calls genuinely failed to cache. Recorded as a measurement plus a
reading. CLOSED with --class plan_defect (the S3 design specified the warning without the cacheability
precondition). It took TWO attempts: the first died on the store lock AFTER the verifier had run.

## NEW BUG f81d-bab0-3938-4f1c — those two warnings are REAL COST BLEED
  step coach_notes, sonnet, input 4538  |  a sub-call, haiku, input 6426  -> both cache_write=0.
Same run, same process, same provider, while the finder calls wrote 5781-9385 each. So not "caching
unavailable" — specific call sites get none, and cache_write=0 means nothing was ever WRITTEN, so
there is no first-call-populates explanation. Root cause NOT established; the ticket says so and
tells the investigator to capture the outbound request rather than read code. Linked discovered_from
7a79. (Noted but NOT asserted as a defect: CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS=4096 is documented as the OPUS
floor yet applied to every model.)

## 48b3 — the scope blocker is RESOLVED, on the plan's own terms
The three assertions in 7de4's test_model_class_ladder.py pinned exactly the behaviour 48b3 removes.
The third test's OWN docstring said "PINNED, deliberately NOT fixed here ... owned by its own
ticket" — 48b3 IS that ticket, and the plan anticipated the handoff but could not name the file
because 7de4 had not landed yet. So extending scope was the plan executing, not widening.
  - two "some-unknown-model" assertions -> primary-alone ladder / ladder-minimum window
  - test_..._foreign_family_is_unchanged RENAMED to _is_explicit (the old name asserted the DEFECT as
    intended behaviour); grepped the tree for the old name, zero remaining refs.
MUTATION-CHECKED: with pre-fix sizing.py all three FAIL (whole ladder / 1000000), restored all GREEN.
file_impact extended to 4 paths. Full suite on the 48b3 tree: 8908 passed, SUITE_EXIT=0.

## d5c7 — a DECISION, deliberately left to the operator
The 5e75 run satisfies AC3 AS WRITTEN (no contract violation, INDETERMINATE 0, findings keep verified
severity) but `empty_outcomes 0` proves the repaired branch NEVER EXECUTED. Per this ticket's own
census (43 violations all zero-finding; 2778 multi-finding runs, zero violations) a run WITH findings
cannot discriminate — citing it would be citing a test that passes on unfixed code. A zero-finding
run is ~1% of history and cannot be commanded. The deterministic proof exists and is green
(test_verify_empty_batch_contract.py, 4 passed). Options recorded on the ticket; I did NOT edit the
AC, because bending an AC to fit the evidence on hand is the failure mode this ticket exists to catch.

## THE STORE LOCK IS A REAL HAZARD — from OTHER sessions, not from mine
`flock: could not acquire lock after 60s` killed a 7a79 close AFTER its verifier had already run
(CLOSE_EXIT=1, sidecar emit failed, ticket stayed in_progress) and dropped a d5c7 comment silently.
Cause identified by ps, not guessed: a concurrent session in /Users/joeoakhart/impl-0303-bridge-state
running `rebar transition f7ee-...` held the global .ticket-write.lock for many minutes, plus a
review-plan from rebar-jira-family. ALWAYS verify a write landed; a shell echo reports success
regardless. The working remedy is a RETRY LOOP that re-reads state each pass and stops when the
change is observed — that is how the d5c7 comment eventually landed.

## THE CLOSING ARC IS BIGGER THAN IT LOOKS
0d76, eb6e and 8625 are ALL `unsigned` — none has a certified plan-review attestation, so each needs
a passing review before it can even be claimed, IN DEPENDENCY ORDER (0d76 first). 0d76's plan
remediation from the prior session never finished: its agent died mid-round-4 on an API error, and
the ticket still shows 8 comments with the Bedrock attestation intact but the plan unrevised. Its
remaining operator-attested criterion is a paired-run ParityReport — unblocked, since Bedrock
invokability is proven, but not yet done.

## GERRIT
Nothing from this epic is open. The three open changes (1219 ce5d, 1220/1221 d067) belong to other
tickets; d067 SUBMITTED mid-session, so origin/main moved 144bb02 -> 2ea5c3391d under me. Re-derive
refs; do not assume the tip you fetched is still the tip.
Pre-merge commits were CHERRY-PICKED onto current main, never rebased — their parents were SHA-
rewritten by Gerrit on submit. Backups: backup/48b3-premerge, backup/77ed-premerge.
